'''Bonita Valerie Saunders''' is an American mathematician specializing in [[mathematical visualization]]. She works at the [[National Institute of Standards and Technology]] in the Applied and Computational Mathematics Division of the Information Technology Laboratory, where she contributes to the [[Digital Library of Mathematical Functions]] as the Visualization Editor and the principal designer of visualizations and graphs.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=DLMF: Bonita V. Saunders|url=https://dlmf.nist.gov/about/bio/BVSaunders|url-status=live|access-date=2020-06-30|website=dlmf.nist.gov|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091231065444/http://dlmf.nist.gov:80/about/bio/BVSaunders |archive-date=2009-12-31 }}</ref>

== Professional career ==
Saunders received her Ph.D. in computational and applied mathematics from [[Old Dominion University]] in 1985.<ref name=":0" /> She earned her M.S. in Mathematics from the [[University of Virginia]] and her B.A. in Mathematics from the College of William and Mary.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=Bonita V. Saunders, Mathematician of the African Diaspora|url=https://www.math.buffalo.edu/mad/PEEPS/saunders_bonitav.html|access-date=2020-07-14|website=www.math.buffalo.edu}}</ref>  She worked at the BDM corporation for four years and has published a number of papers.<ref name=":1" /> A list of her papers can be found at the [[DBLP|dblp]] "Computer Science" bibliography.[https://dblp.org/pers/s/Saunders:Bonita_V=.html] Her current research interests include, "Visualization of Complex Functions Data, Numerical Software for Special Functions, Numerical Grid Generation, [and] Numerical Solution of Partial Differential Equations."<ref>{{Cite web|date=September 25, 2020|title=Bonita V. Saunders|url=https://math.nist.gov/~BSaunders/|url-status=live|access-date=2021-10-26|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20000823004323/http://math.nist.gov:80/~BSaunders/ |archive-date=2000-08-23 }}</ref>

Saunders has made a number of contributions to the [[Mathematical Association of America]] (MAA).  From 1999 to 2002, she served as the MD-DC-VA Section treasurer.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=Mathematical Association of America - Maryland-District of Columbia-Virginia Section|url=http://sections.maa.org/mddcva/Fall2019Meeting.php|access-date=2020-07-14|website=sections.maa.org}}</ref>  From 2004 to 2009, she was on the selection committee for the Etta Z. Falconer Lecture (sponsored by the MAA and the [[Association for Women in Mathematics|Association for Women in Mathematics AWM]]).<ref name=":2" />  She was also on the MAA Business Industry Government Committee from 2012-2017,<ref name=":2" /> and was the MD-DC-VA Section Representative to the MAA Congress in 2019.<ref name=":2" />  As of 2020 she is on the editorial board for Mathematics Magazine<ref name=":2" /> and the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] (SIAM) Board of Trustees.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Leadership {{!}} SIAM|url=https://www.siam.org/about-siam/leadership|access-date=2021-07-11|website=www.siam.org}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
The National Association of Mathematicians chose Saunders to give the 2001 Claytor Lecture at the [[Joint Mathematics Meetings]].<ref name=":0" />

The US Department of Commerce awarded her research group a Gold Medal for Distinguished Scientific/Engineering Achievement in 2011, in recognition for her work in creating the online Digital Library of Mathematical Functions.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=United States Department of Commerce Sixty-Third Annual Honor Awards Program|url=https://www.commerce.gov/sites/default/files/2018-12/2011-Annual-Honor-Awards-Program-Book.pdf|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200630214201/https://www.commerce.gov/sites/default/files/2018-12/2011-Annual-Honor-Awards-Program-Book.pdf |archive-date=2020-06-30 |access-date=|website=}}</ref>

In 2017, Saunders was awarded the NIST Information Technology Laboratory Outstanding Contribution Award for Excellence in Technical Leadership.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Bonita V. Saunders Named 2021 AWM-MAA Falconer Lecturer|work=AWM Newsletter|url=https://awm-math.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/AWM-News-July-Aug-2021-WEB.pdf}}</ref>

In 2018, [[Mathematically Gifted & Black]] made Saunders a Black History Month honoree.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Bonita V. Saunders|url=https://mathematicallygiftedandblack.com/honorees/bonita-v-saunders/|access-date=2020-06-30|website=Mathematically Gifted & Black|language=en-US}}</ref>

In 2019 she accepted the Excellence in Research in Mathematics and Computer Science award from the Washington Academy of Sciences<ref>{{Cite web|title=Awards Banquet 2019 - Washington Academy of Sciences|url=https://www.washacadsci.org/awards-banquet-2019/|access-date=2020-06-30|language=en-US}}</ref> and became a Fellow of the Washington Academy of Sciences.<ref name=":0" />

Saunders gave the 2021 AWM-MAA [[Etta Zuber Falconer]] Lecture at [[MathFest]] 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|title=AWM-MAA Etta Falconer Lecture 2020-2021|url=https://awm-math.org/awards/falconer-lectures/falconer-lecture-2020/|url-status=live|website=Association for Women in Mathematics|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210604104554/https://awm-math.org/awards/falconer-lectures/falconer-lecture-2020/ |archive-date=2021-06-04 }}</ref>
